Part I — Knowledge Base (English)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Knowledge Base (Session 41, English)
The Complete Pitru Cycle: Subtle Bodies, Kul Devta vs. Ancestors, and the Power of Ram Naam at the Moment of Death

Sour ce: a live Ashaeiynn satsang opening with standing guidance on aura-checking practice and independence-focused bhakti, moving into an extended, heavily interactive teaching on how the "pitru cycle" (ancestor subtle-body mechanics) actually works — tarpan, photo-worship, and coconut-invocation rituals explained mechanistically — the categorical differ ence between kul devta and pitru, why saints' subtle bodies ar e naturally pr otected, and the r eal mechanism behind chanting Ram naam at the moment of death.
1. Standing Practice Note: Aura-Checking and Today's Format

1. Bhaiya opens by noting that full aura-checking (ora checking) has no fixed limit — shaktipaat alone takes mentors three to four days per person to properly assess and track aura status, plus the current day's session, totaling roughly five days of aurachecking work already done for this group. 2. Bhaiya states that on formal session days like this one, the practice is to set aside aura-checking and instead discuss subtle-world (sookshma jagat) facts and secr et knowledge (gupt vidyaen) that will specifically become useful once a person's third eye (third drishti) has opened — covering how to see, how to learn, how subtle-world sciences work, how to communicate from there, and how to establish standing within it. 3. A cor e supporting pr emise repeated her e: the physical world is only a manifestation of the astral world ("physical world is only a manifestation of astral world") — without investment in the subtle world, nothing is truly attainable in the physical world.
2. A Message to Pur ely Devotional Bhakts (No Drishti, No Dietary Discipline)

1. Bhaiya addr esses those who chant God's name constantly , trust in God completely , and don't concern themselves with dietary purity , drishti, or other attainments — only wanting bhakti (devotion) itself. He honors this as a valid, even superior path, noting his own foundational identity is as "a small devotee" first, before any third-eye-focused work. 2. A specific claim: if someone's name is spoken 21 times thr ough Sri Hanuman Ji Maharaj's own mouth, a str eam of siddhis (spiritual accomplishments) begins trailing that person — their speech gains "sthirta" (stability/steadiness), and the person begins to spontaneously become "siddha." 3. Definition of "siddha" offer ed here: a person is called siddha when their speech itself carries siddhata (accomplishmentpower) — whatever task they touch or whatever statement they make begins to spontaneously succeed or come true.
3. Two Paths to Ashaeiynn: Drishti-Seekers vs. Bhakti-Seekers

1. Bhaiya distinguishes two types of people who come to him: some come specifically for drishti (third-eye sight), others come pur ely for bhakti (devotion). Drawing on his own direct experience over his years running Ashaeiynn, he notes that many who once had visible drishti/could see subtle-world things eventually got "stuck" at some plateau.

2. By contrast, pur ely devotional people who came only for bhakti — without initially seeking drishti — have since become mentors, now speaking dir ectly with Hanuman Ji Maharaj themselves. Bhaiya includes himself in this category , referring to himself informally as one of the "crazy ones" who were simply devoted to God and ended up becoming a mentor this way .
4. "Being Told" vs. "Seeing Dir ectly" — Two Differ ent Mechanisms

1. A key distinction: having something told/r evealed to you (batana) is categorically differ ent from dir ectly seeing it through your own drishti. Bhaiya illustrates this using Bageshwar Dham's Dhirendra Shastri, who this teaching states does not personally have drishti — rather , he is told things by his own ancestral (pitru) lineage, which has been actively working on his behalf for roughly 300 years across three generations, accumulating deep astral-world knowledge in the process. 2. The same pattern is attributed to the Pithadhikshak (head) of Pandokar Sarkar — no personal drishti, but told things by a similarly multi-generational, highly accomplished pitru lineage that has, over time, ef fectively become "kings" of the astral world through sustained practice. 3. By contrast, this teaching states that Sri Hanuman Ji Maharaj's specific grace at Ashaeiynn teaches a vidya wher e practitioners use drishti dir ectly alongside understanding astral-world truths themselves — becoming fully self-suf ficient (sarv samarth), able to communicate directly with devtas via their own drishti, and able to identify and cut any bandhan (binding), curse, or negative ener gy af fecting themselves or their family without needing to depend on anyone else.
5. Why "Middle-Class" Families Lack This Kind of Ancestral Support

1. This teaching explains why families like Dhir endra Shastri's or Pandokar Sarkar's have such str ong pitru backing: their ancestors have been actively practicing/working in the astral world for three generations (r oughly 300 years), accumulating deep knowledge. Ordinary "middle-class" families (Bhaiya's own audience, by his own description) typically have no such multi-generational astral-working lineage. 2. Bhaiya uses a vivid analogy: "we get gr ound up like almonds and pistachios" — meaning ordinary middle-class people ar e exploited/drained specifically because those above them (with str onger pitru-backing) ar e actively working the astral-world systems, while ordinary families r emain "educated but blind" (padhe likhe andhe), lacking drishti, reacting only after problems appear and depending on whichever family member is known to "sense" things.
6. Why Everyone Must Learn to See for Themselves

1. Bhaiya's central practical instruction: since "being told" only extends as far as the teller's own knowledge, every practitioner — regardless of education or car eer status — must personally learn to open their own drishti and understand astral-world mechanics dir ectly , rather than r emaining permanently dependent on someone else's word. 2. Because middle-class families typically lack inherited astral-working ancestors, this teaching states their required personal effort is necessarily higher: each person must effectively become the "pitru" who does this work for their own descendants, since no one alr eady occupies that r ole for them. 3. A candid observation: very few people ar e actually willing to put in the effort to learn this themselves — most people who approach Bhaiya want a fast, transactional fix ("here's ₹5,000, ₹10,000, just tell me the remedy") rather than genuine instruction. Bhaiya states his explicit teaching philosophy is the reverse: "I am teaching you to see your own pr oblem, not solving it for you." 4. Bhaiya r eferences a specific mandate fr om his own guru: to personally train 100 people equipped with compr ehensive knowledge of these vidyas, capable of altering planetary and elemental influences (graha-nakshatra aur tatvon ki chaal) in their own lives thr ough their own effort.
7. Learning as a Generational, Lifelong Investment

1. Bhaiya frames this learning as pr oducing lasting, transferable pr otection: someone who has genuinely learned these vidyas will instantly r ecognize and be able to cut any tantrik kriya (magical attack) aimed at their children, both during

their own lifetime and — since a well-developed independent subtle body continues functioning after physical death — even after they pass away . 2. A direct, personal statement r evealing Bhaiya's own given name in this teaching: "Ek Parikshit Bhaiya kaafi nahi hai" ("one Parikshit Bhaiya isn't enough for you") — meaning practitioners cannot r emain permanently dependent on Bhaiya himself and must build this capability personally , since he cannot pr ovide unlimited one-on-one pr oblem-solving to every member indefinitely .
8. The Mechanics of the "Pitru Cycle": What Actually Happens After Death

1. When a physical body dies, the prana/atma tattva (soul-element) instantly merges back into the paramatma tattva (universal divine essence) — this is the true meaning of a soul "becoming one" with the divine at death. 2. However , a separate element r emains after this merging: the sookshma sharir (subtle body) — described as what is popularly called "the soul" in modern-day language, though this teaching distinguishes it clearly from the atma tattva that has already mer ged into the divine. 3. This sookshma sharir is independent and continues r oaming/existing on its own — even while the original atma tattva may take rebirth elsewhere entirely , the subtle body it leaves behind persists as its own separate entity . 4. This is offer ed as the dir ect explanation for why up to ten generations of ancestors can be said to "sit"/persist within a single household — even though souls constantly reincarnate elsewhere, each generation's independent subtle body remains behind and can continue interacting with the living family .
9. Tarpan, Photo-W orship, and the Coconut (Nariyal) Invocation Ritual Explained

1. Regarding tarpan (the ritual water -offering to ancestors): this teaching confirms it is genuine and effective — offerings placed with intention (like water kept near a deceased r elative's photo) genuinely ar e received and consumed by that subtle body , when addr essed corr ectly . 2. The formal panda/pandit-led post-death ritual of "seating" (bithana) a r estless ancestor's subtle body onto a coconut or a small wooden/stone murti is explained as a practical anchoring technique — since an unsettled subtle body may otherwise wander and disturb the living household, this ritual uses grahan shakti (a specific channeling/receiving technique) to draw and stabilize that particular subtle body onto a fixed object.
10. Four Scenarios of What Actually Happens When You Pray to an Ancestor's Photo

1. Scenario one — a genuine, willing ancestor: if the subtle body being addr essed is genuinely that ancestor and it is willing, the pranam (offering of r espect) reaches it instantly , since subtle bodies in the astral world ar e highly "active"/r esponsive — of ferings reach lower -level (pret-type) entities especially quickly , since the of ferer and the pret exist at a broadly similar "level"; by contrast, of ferings don't reach devtas nearly as easily , since devtas occupy a categorically higher level. 2. Scenario two — a "malin" (impur e/degraded) ancestor: if the addr essed pitru's own natur e was impur e or pretnatur ed, then each time it grants a blessing, it is effectively transferring a fragment of its own impur e tattva into the person praying — meaning daily , repeated pranam to such an ancestor can slowly accumulate impurity/"kachra" (garbage) inside the practitioner's own body over time, even though no single instance feels harmful. 3. Scenario thr ee — a "shwet, swachh" (white, pur e) ancestor of gr eat accomplishment: if the addr essed pitru was genuinely pur e and highly accomplished (possessing gr eat shakti and siddhi), daily pranam to them brings no pr oblems whatsoever to that household, ever . 4. Scenario four — a fraudulent stand-in: if, at the moment of prayer , the actual intended ancestor was not pr esent but some unr elated nearby pr et happened to be ther e instead, that pr et can fraudulently r espond "blessing granted" and effectively "become" the person's ancestor going forward — described colorfully as "making someone your father by sheer coincidence" (dhakke se kisi ko baap banana).

5. A specific practical caution r egarding generic invocation: addr essing prayers to "sarv pitr o bhay namah" (a blanket bow to all ancestors, without a specific name) indiscriminately sweeps in this same "garbage" risk, since it fails to distinguish a genuinely worthy ancestor from an unr elated or impure entity that happens to r espond.
1 1. Kul Devta and Pitru Are Categorically Differ ent — Never Conflate Them

1. A direct sangat question addr essed this session: is a family's kul devta simply its most powerful/accomplished ancestor (pitru)? This teaching answers firmly no — devta is devta, and pitru/pr et is pitru/pret; these ar e categorically distinct classes of being, and a kul devta specifically is never "just" an unusually str ong ancestor . 2. However , this teaching acknowledges that some ambitious or powerful pitru can falsely pr esent themselves as a family's kul devta ("kul devta ban ke aa jaate hain"), effectively impersonating that r ole for a time. This teaching states plainly that on the day the genuine kul devta actually shows up, any such impersonating pitru will be immediately exposed and destroyed ("un pitron ki thatri ban jaayegi").
12. Energy Can Only Be Generated by a Living Physical Body

1. This teaching's cor e mechanical claim: spiritual/astral energy (urja) can only be generated by a living human body possessing all five elements — even devtas are described as needing a human body to act through and generate ener gy in the physical world; a person's own body is what actively produces and radiates this ener gy while alive. 2. Once the physical body separates fr om the subtle body at death, energy generation stops entir ely — "jitna katora tumhare paas hai utna hi rahega" ("whatever bowl/capacity you've accumulated is all you'll ever have") — meaning no further spiritual capacity can be built after death; whatever was accumulated during physical life is final.
13. The Real Mechanism Behind Chanting Ram Naam at the Moment of Death

1. A direct sangat question: does chanting "Ram" at the moment of death guarantee liberation/r escue for the dying person? This teaching's answer: it can genuinely help, but not because it generates new energy — since, per the previous section, only a living body can generate energy , and a dying/dead body cannot. 2. The actual mechanism explained: if a person says "Ram" (even involuntarily — such as crying out the name by chance, or having it whisper ed into their ear by someone nearby) at the moment of death, that name tends to r emain their last, most vivid memory , and their subtle body may continue r epeating "Ram Ram Ram" afterward pur ely out of habitual memory , without generating any new energy of its own. 3. Because countless generations of devotees have chanted Ram naam, this teaching states ther e ar e corr espondingly vast numbers of accomplished subtle bodies/saints still actively "r oaming" who ar e themselves devoted to that same name — and one of these may notice a newly wandering subtle body still r epeating "Ram Ram" and choose to "adopt" it, offering it pr otection and a portion of their own accumulated energy , purely out of shar ed devotion to the same name. 4. Bhaiya's own stated commitment illustrating this principle: "we don't let a living Ram devotee go hungry — how would we let one go unpr otected after death?" — framing the rescue as an act of hospitality/adoption by an existing accomplished subtle body , not a mechanical result of the dying person's own final utterance. 5. This is offer ed as the deeper explanation for Ram naam's immense glory (mahima): because it has been chanted acr oss so many generations, an enormous population of subtle bodies exists that ar e permanently devoted to that specific name — meaning anyone found still r epeating it at the moment of death has a very high likelihood of being found and aided by one of them.
14. Common Beliefs About Auspicious Death-Days Are Rejected

1. This teaching dir ectly r ejects the popular belief that dying on a specific "auspicious" day (such as Nirjala Ekadashi) has any special positive effect on a person's afterlife journey — described plainly as "just stories." 2. The actual effect of auspicious days like Diwali or Shivratri, per this teaching, is entir ely about the living: on such days, universal cosmic energy incr eases dramatically , which specifically amplifies a living yogi or sadhak's own grahan shakti

(receiving/channeling capacity) — it has zer o effect on people who ar e alr eady dead. 3. Similarly , the popular belief that Bhagwan Krishna personally escorts anyone who dies on Janmashtami is dir ectly rejected using a "common sense" argument: if this wer e true, given how many people die on any given day , Krishna would effectively need to personally escort people "every single day ," not just once a year — so either the belief or the specific day's supposed significance must be false. 4. The folk belief that a cr ow eating offer ed rice confirms an ancestor's satisfaction/acceptance is likewise dismissed as "just a story ," in the same category as the pr evious two r ejected beliefs.
15. Why Saints' Subtle Bodies Remain Naturally Pr otected Fr om Negativity

1. A sangat question on why negativity doesn't appr oach saints/mahatmas is answer ed mechanically: a saint's subtle body is alr eady in a constant, intensely "blazing" state (sookshma jal raha hota hai) due to sustained tapasya, and nothing can appr oach or attach to something alr eady burning at that intensity . 2. Bhaiya's illustrative self-comparison: "if my entir e subtle body is nothing but fir e, who's going to come near me?" — versus a subtle body that is instead richly bejeweled and unguarded, like a king riding out alone cover ed in jewels, which this teaching states would be "looted" within an hour , in both the physical and astral worlds alike. 3. This is offer ed as the dir ect justification for why so much personal jaap (mantra chanting) is pr escribed on top of hawan: hawan r emoves existing negativity fr om the body , but only sustained jaap can r efill that emptied space with protective energy — otherwise, something else will move into the vacated space instead.
16. Boundaries on What This Teaching Will Personally Explain

1. Bhaiya explicitly declines to personally answer certain specific ritual questions this session (for example, the pr ecise subtle mechanics of a gau-pujan/cow-worship cer emony performed at weddings), instead r edirecting practitioners to open their own third eye and observe such things dir ectly for themselves, then r eport back what they find. 2. When asked about a specific minimum jaap count, Bhaiya gives a concr ete practical minimum: at least 500 r epetitions per session as a baseline.
17. Kul Devta Changes After Marriage — For the Person Marrying In

1. A direct sangat question fr om a woman: does her kul devta change after marriage to that of her husband's family? This teaching answers yes — by taking agni (sacr ed fire) as witness during the wedding cer emony (saptapadi), a woman's kul devta shifts to her husband's family's kul devta going forward. 2. This teaching clarifies that no separate "r elease" ritual is needed for her natal family's kul devta — since taking agni as witness in marriage alr eady constitutes having formally left that original household/gotra, the transition is automatically complete thr ough the wedding ritual itself.
QUICK RULES SUMMARY

The physical world is only a manifestation of the astral world — real, lasting progress in physical life requires genuine investment/practice in the subtle (astral) world first. "Being told" something (batana) and "seeing it dir ectly" via one's own drishti (dikhna) ar e two categorically differ ent mechanisms — families like Dhirendra Shastri's or Pandokar Sarkar's rely on multi-generational ancestor (pitru) guidance rather than personal drishti; this teaching's own method trains practitioners to see and act independently instead. Every practitioner must eventually learn to open their own drishti and understand astral mechanics dir ectly — depending permanently on being told things by someone else (including Bhaiya himself) has an inherent ceiling; "one Parikshit Bhaiya isn't enough" for lifelong dependency .

At death, the atma tattva (soul-element) instantly merges into the paramatma, but a separate, independent sookshma sharir (subtle body) r emains behind and continues existing on its own — this is why multiple generations of ancestors can persist and interact within a single household. Tarpan and ancestor photo-worship ar e real and effective, but carry four distinct possible outcomes depending on whether the addressed entity is a genuine willing ancestor , an impure ("malin") ancestor , a pure and accomplished ancestor , or an unrelated pret fraudulently standing in — always address ancestors specifically by name rather than generically , to reduce this risk. Kul devta and pitru (ancestor) ar e categorically differ ent classes of being — never conflate them — though an ambitious pitru can sometimes falsely impersonate a kul devta role until the real kul devta arrives and exposes the impersonation. Spiritual energy (urja) can only be generated by a living physical body — ener gy generation stops permanently at death; whatever spiritual "capacity" was built during life is final and cannot be increased afterward. Chanting "Ram" at the moment of death can genuinely help, but not by generating new energy — it works because countless accomplished subtle bodies devoted to that same name may notice and "adopt" a subtle body still repeating it, of fering protection out of shared devotion. Popular beliefs about auspicious death-days (Nirjala Ekadashi), Janmashtami-specific divine escorts, and cr ows confirming ancestor satisfaction ar e all dir ectly r ejected as folklor e — auspicious days only amplify living practitioners' own receiving capacity , with zero ef fect on the already-deceased. Saints' subtle bodies r emain naturally pr otected because they ar e constantly "blazing" fr om sustained tapasya — this is why consistent personal jaap (not hawan alone) is essential: hawan clears negativity , but only ongoing jaap refills that space with protection. A woman's kul devta shifts to her husband's family's kul devta upon marriage, automatically , through taking agni as witness — no separate release ritual is needed for her natal family's kul devta. Spelling note: the institute's name is written "Ashaeiynn" — use this spelling consistently .
Part II — Q&A Pairs (English)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Q&A Pairs (Session 41, English)
The Complete Pitru Cycle: Subtle Bodies, Kul Devta vs. Ancestors, and the Power of Ram Naam at the Moment of Death
User-style questions with answers gr ounded in this Ashaeiynn live session. Gr eeting style: "Jai Siya Ram."

Q1. How long does full aura-checking actually take, per this teaching? A: Per this teaching, there's no fixed limit — mentors typically take three to four days per person to properly assess and track aura status, and this session's group had roughly five days of aura-checking work already completed before this class.

Q2. Why does Bhaiya sometimes set aside aura-checking during a formal session? A: On formal session days, the practice is to instead discuss subtle-world (sookshma jagat) facts and secret knowledge specifically useful once a person's third eye has opened — covering how to see, learn, communicate, and establish standing within the astral world.

Q3. What's the r elationship between the physical world and the astral (subtle) world, per this teaching? A: The physical world is described as only a manifestation of the astral world — without investment in the subtle world, nothing is truly attainable in the physical world.

Q4. Does this teaching look down on devotees who just chant God's name without seeking drishti or worrying about dietary discipline? A: No — Bhaiya honors this as a valid, even foundational path, stating his own base identity is as "a small devotee" first, before any third-eye-focused work.

Q5. What happens if someone's name is spoken 21 times thr ough Hanuman Ji Maharaj's own mouth? A: Per this teaching, a stream of siddhis (spiritual accomplishments) begins trailing that person — their speech gains stability (sthirta), and they begin spontaneously becoming "siddha."

Q6. What does "siddha" actually mean, per this teaching? A: A person is called siddha when their speech itself carries siddhata (accomplishment-power) — whatever task they touch, or whatever they state, begins to spontaneously succeed or come true.

Q7. Are there different reasons people come to Ashaeiynn? A: Yes — some come specifically seeking drishti (third-eye sight), others come purely for bhakti (devotion). Bhaiya notes from direct experience that many who once had visible drishti eventually got "stuck" at some plateau, while purely devotional seekers have gone on to become mentors, speaking directly with Hanuman Ji Maharaj.

Q8. What's the differ ence between having something "told" to you and "seeing" it dir ectly? A: Per this teaching, these are categorically dif ferent mechanisms. Being told relies on someone else's (or some lineage's) accumulated knowledge being relayed to you; seeing directly means perceiving astral-world truths yourself through your own drishti.

Q9. Does Bageshwar Dham's Dhir endra Shastri have drishti, according to this teaching? A: No — per this teaching, he doesn't personally have drishti; he is told things by his own ancestral (pitru) lineage, which has reportedly been actively working on his behalf for roughly 300 years across three generations, accumulating deep astral knowledge in the process.

Q10. Is the same true of Pandokar Sarkar's Pithadhikshak? A: Yes — this teaching attributes the same pattern to them: no personal drishti, but guidance from a similarly multi-generational, highly accomplished pitru lineage that has ef fectively become astral-world "royalty" through generations of sustained practice.

Q1 1. What makes Ashaeiynn's appr oach differ ent from r elying on inherited pitru guidance? A: Per this teaching, Hanuman Ji Maharaj's specific grace here teaches practitioners to use drishti directly alongside understanding astral truths themselves — becoming fully self-suf ficient, able to communicate with devtas directly and cut any bandhan or negative ener gy without depending on anyone else.

Q12. Why do "middle-class" families lack this kind of powerful ancestral backing? A: Per this teaching, families like Dhirendra Shastri's or Pandokar Sarkar's benefit from three generations (roughly 300 years) of actively working, knowledge-accumulating ancestors — an inheritance most ordinary families simply don't have.

Q13. What's Bhaiya's analogy for how ordinary middle-class people get exploited spiritually? A: "We get ground up like almonds and pistachios" — meaning middle-class families are drained specifically because those with stronger inherited pitru-backing are actively working astral-world systems, while ordinary families remain "educated but blind" (padhe likhe andhe), reacting only after problems appear .

Q14. Why does this teaching insist everyone must learn to see for themselves rather than just being told things? A: Because being told only extends as far as the teller's own knowledge — so every practitioner , regardless of education or career status, must personally learn to open their own drishti and understand astral mechanics directly to avoid permanent dependency .

Q15. Since middle-class families usually lack an inherited astral-working lineage, what does this mean practically? A: Per this teaching, their required personal ef fort is necessarily higher — each person must ef fectively become the "pitru" who does this protective work for their own descendants, since no one already occupies that role for them.

Q16. Are most people willing to actually put in this effort? A: Per this teaching, very few — most people who approach Bhaiya want a fast, transactional fix ("here's money , just tell me the remedy") rather than genuine instruction. Bhaiya's stated philosophy is the reverse: teaching people to see their own problem, not solving it for them.

Q17. What mandate does Bhaiya say his own guru gave him? A: To personally train 100 people equipped with comprehensive knowledge of these vidyas — people capable of altering planetary and elemental influences in their own lives through their own ef fort.

Q18. What's the long-term payoff of genuinely learning these vidyas, per this teaching? A: Someone who has truly learned will instantly recognize and be able to cut any tantrik kriya aimed at their children — both during their own lifetime, and even after death, since a well-developed independent subtle body continues functioning after physical death.

Q19. Does Bhaiya r eveal anything about his own personal identity in this session? A: Yes — he states directly , "Ek Parikshit Bhaiya kaafi nahi hai" ("one Parikshit Bhaiya isn't enough for you"), revealing his own given name (Parikshit) while emphasizing that practitioners cannot remain permanently dependent on him alone.

Q20. What actually happens to a person's soul at the moment of physical death? A: Per this teaching, the prana/atma tattva instantly mer ges back into the paramatma tattva (universal divine essence) — this is the true meaning of a soul "becoming one" with the divine at death.

Q21. If the soul merges into the divine, what is commonly called "the soul" that people talk about afterward — ghosts, ancestors, etc.? A: Per this teaching, that's actually the sookshma sharir (subtle body) — a separate element that remains behind after the atma tattva mer ges into paramatma. It's independent and continues existing/roaming on its own, even while the original atma tattva may take rebirth elsewhere entirely .

Q22. How can up to ten generations of ancestors all persist within one household if souls keep r eincarnating? A: Because each generation's independent subtle body (sookshma sharir) remains behind even after its associated soul (atma tattva) reincarnates
elsewhere — the two are separate, and it's the subtle body that continues interacting with the living family .

Q23. Is tarpan (the ancestor water -offering ritual) actually effective, per this teaching? A: Yes — this teaching confirms it's genuine; of ferings placed with intention (like water kept near a photo) are genuinely received and consumed by the addressed subtle body , when addressed correctly .

Q24. What's the actual purpose of the panda-led ritual of "seating" a r estless ancestor on a coconut or small murti? A: Per this teaching, it's a practical anchoring technique using grahan shakti (a channeling/receiving method) to draw and stabilize an unsettled ancestor's subtle body onto a fixed object, preventing it from wandering and disturbing the living household.

Q25. What actually happens when I pray to a deceased r elative's photo — is it always my actual ancestor responding? A: Not necessarily — this teaching describes four scenarios: (1) a genuine, willing ancestor receives your pranam instantly , since subtle bodies are highly responsive to those at a similar "level"; (2) an impure ("malin") ancestor's blessing actually transfers a fragment of its own impurity into you over repeated prayers; (3) a genuinely pure, accomplished ancestor's daily pranam brings no problems ever; (4) if no actual ancestor was present, an unrelated nearby pret can fraudulently respond and ef fectively "become" your ancestor from then on.

Q26. Is ther e a safer way to addr ess ancestors in prayer to avoid the "fraudulent stand-in" risk? A: Per this teaching, addressing prayers to a specific named ancestor is safer than a generic blanket address like "sarv pitro bhay namah" (bowing to all ancestors without specifying), which indiscriminately sweeps in whatever "garbage" happens to respond.

Q27. Is a family's kul devta just its most powerful ancestor? A: No — this teaching answers firmly that devta and pitru/pret are categorically dif ferent classes of being; a kul devta is never simply an unusually strong ancestor , even though some ambitious pitru can temporarily falsely impersonate that role until the genuine kul devta arrives and exposes them.

Q28. Can spiritual energy be generated after death? A: No — per this teaching, ener gy (urja) can only be generated by a living physical body possessing all five elements; even devtas need a human body to act through. Once body and subtle body separate at death, ener gy generation stops permanently — whatever capacity was built during life is final.

Q29. Does chanting "Ram" at the moment of death guarantee liberation? A: Not automatically through generating new ener gy — since a dying/dead body can't generate ener gy . But per this teaching it can genuinely help through a dif ferent mechanism: the dying person's subtle body may continue repeating "Ram Ram" out of habitual memory , and an existing accomplished subtle body/saint devoted to that same name may notice and "adopt" it, of fering protection and shared ener gy purely out of devotional kinship.

Q30. Why does Ram naam specifically carry such immense glory (mahima), per this teaching? A: Because it has been chanted across countless generations, an enormous population of subtle bodies remains permanently devoted to that name — so anyone found still repeating it at death has a very high likelihood of being noticed and rescued by one of them.
